description: TDD blueprint for the Journey Builder feature: command/ribbon launch shows a welcome screen with Create New / Open Existing choices. Create a journey with name, description, start event, steps with actions, end event, then export to JSON + canvas.

improvements.title: Attach vault notes to journey steps
improvements.description: Allow attaching vault notes to the journey or individual steps, either via autosuggest (file picker) or by adding them like goals in the session view (Enter to add, x to remove). Notes give context to what each step tests or references.

improvements.title: Build-only option in interactive session view
improvements.description: Added 'd) Build only' to the session view menu. Quick-builds and deploys to the test vault without re-running tests, then returns to the same session view.

setup.title: Ensure clean workspace
setup.description: Closes stale Journey Builder leaves and modals from previous runs.

actions.description: Close stale Journey Builder sidebar leaves

steps.title: Open Journey Builder via command
steps.description: Executes the flowti:open-journey-builder command. Verifies the sidebar leaf opens, then closes it for the ribbon test.
steps.expectedInput: Plugin enabled, no active Journey Builder instance

actions.message: Step 1/5: Opening Journey Builder via command

actions.description: Open Journey Builder via command palette

steps.title: Open Journey Builder via ribbon
steps.description: Clicks the Journey Builder ribbon button. Sidebar opens on the right with welcome screen showing Create New and Open Existing cards.
steps.expectedOutput: Journey Builder sidebar leaf exists with welcome screen visible in right pane

actions.message: Step 2/5: Opening Journey Builder via ribbon

actions.code: (() => { const leaves = app.workspace.getLeavesOfType('flowti-journey-builder'); if (leaves.length === 0) return 'none'; const leaf = leaves[0]; return leaf.getRoot() === app.workspace.rightSplit ? 'right' : 'other'; })()
actions.description: Sidebar is in the right split pane

actions.instruction: Verify the ribbon button has a route icon. The sidebar should appear in the right pane with two action cards: Open Existing Journey and Create New Journey.

steps.title: Create a new journey via setup form
steps.description: Clicks Create New Journey. The sidebar transitions to a setup form where the user enters journey name, description, and start event.
steps.expectedInput: Journey Builder sidebar open with welcome screen
steps.expectedOutput: Setup form visible with metadata fields populated

actions.value: A demo journey created by the Journey Builder.

actions.instruction: Verify the setup form shows journey name, description, and start event fields all filled in. A back button and continue button should be visible.

steps.title: Add a step to the journey
steps.description: Clicks Continue to enter the step builder. Adds a step with a title, confirms it, then sets the end event.
steps.expectedInput: Journey Builder setup form filled with metadata
steps.expectedOutput: Step builder visible with one step card, end event set

actions.description: Click Continue to enter step builder

actions.label: step-added
actions.description: Step added with end event set

actions.instruction: Verify a step card appeared with number badge '1' and title 'Open the user hub'. The end event field should show 'hub.tab.changed'. An export button should be visible at the bottom.

steps.title: Export journey JSON
steps.description: Clicks the Export button. The sidebar emits journey-builder.exported. Once JourneyBuilderService is wired up, it will write the .json file via IFileSystemClient and the EventBridge adapter fallback.
steps.expectedInput: Journey Builder with metadata, start event, one step, and end event
steps.expectedOutput: journey-builder.exported event emitted with full definition payload

improvements.title: Wire up JourneyBuilderService to plugin lifecycle
improvements.description: Start JourneyBuilderService in main.ts so it listens for journey-builder.exported and writes the .json file via IFileSystemClient. Once wired, add file.create.request and file.create.response event assertions.

improvements.title: Generate companion canvas on export
improvements.description: On export, also generate a .canvas file that mirrors the journey structure — start node, step nodes, end node, connected by edges. Same layout as the journey-runner produces after a test run.

actions.instruction: Verify that the export event was emitted. Once JourneyBuilderService is wired up, the event trace will also show file.create.request and file.create.response confirming the JSON was written via the adapter.

teardown.title: Close builder and clean up
teardown.description: Closes the Journey Builder sidebar and modals.
